title: Lending tables show downward shifts with a plus sign
description:
The "Lending decisions: all thirteen nationalities" table on the nationality page prints each shift as a positive number with a plus sign (for example "+4.57" for Laya on American), but the underlying data records the direction as down (direction.signed_pts is -4.57: the model is less confident in approving the loan than for the control version). A reader naturally takes "+" to mean the model is more confident. The same "beyond the control edit" pattern appears in other matrix and board components (site/src/components/Matrix.astro, Board.astro, site/src/scripts/charts.js), so any cell with a downward shift may carry the same misleading sign.

Fix:
- Where a finding has a direction, display the signed value (or the magnitude with the direction in words, e.g. "4.6 lower"), never a "+" on a downward shift.
- Keep magnitude-only displays (stereotype scores with no direction) unchanged, but without a leading "+".
- Keep the aria-label text consistent with the visible value.

Acceptance:
Scenario: downward shift is shown as downward
  Given Laya's small-business-loan shift for American has signed_pts -4.57
  When a reader views the nationality lending table
  Then the cell reads as a decrease, not "+4.57"
Scenario: no stray plus signs
  When the site is built
  Then a test fails if any cell whose direction is "down" renders with a leading "+"
